reviews.title: Poor feedback / contact
reviews.text:
I actually do appreciate Opal, in general. It’s definitely helped me cut down on screentime. Was disappointed tho, that they’re taking the typical bogus approach to customer service by making themselves as unreachable to customers as possible. All I wanted was to send a quick message to the design team, and got stuck in some loop of community forums. I am not wasting my time on that BS. Seems rather ironic that a company claiming to help keep people off their screens would add layers of app garbage for what could just be a simple contact form— click and send. Disappointing. 

And all I had to say, as feedback, was that the backdrop has switched to an ocean scene, but it’s clearly something like AI. The sound doesn’t align with the scene, and it’s clearly a split screen-the same waves mirrored on both sides. Believe me, your customers do spend enough time in nature to know the difference between real ocean and fake. And I will not support AI in any way shape or form, so if this continues, you’ll have lost me. 

There’s also no way to mute the fake ocean sounds. If I’m checking my apps in public, I don’t need extra noise. Design a way to permanently mute the sounds in settings. And don’t waste our time with useless customer service blocks. It just tells me you’re eating up over $100 a year without wanting to actually serve your customers.

reviews.title: I miss the old Opal
reviews.text:
I don’t ever write reviews, but I just want to say when I found opal it was the best app I’ve ever downloaded. It was perfect for screen time monitoring and blocking. It used to be very easy to use and navigate. You used to be able to organize your apps by least to most distracting and also remove certain apps like Navigation/GPS or Music from your screen time. 

Now, everything is counted in your screen time, and even if I’m not using an app but it’s running in the background, like Life360, it counts that as screen time, which, sorry, is kind of absurd. I’m obviously not scrolling on life360 for fourteen hours. 

Also, since the big Opal update a few weeks or months back, certain features just haven’t been working as they used to, and the interface is much more confusing. Sometimes my gems don’t show up on the Home Screen— it’s just empty. For a few days my streak was set back to zero (which was fixed). The app is much more laggy now and sometimes crashes when I try to open it or when I try to unblock an app temporarily. 

One more thing— if you have a time limit rule for an app, say you set YouTube to be allowed for an hour a day, it seems that Opal just counts down from the time that you open the app now rather than monitoring when you’re on or off the app. I personally set my YouTube for 30 mins on certain days, and even if I just open it, watch a video, and exit the app, I’ll still get a notification a half hour later saying that it’s blocked again. 

There’s also a bug or glitch with that particular YouTube rule I think because when it notifies me for “15 mins left” it spams that notification and my phone keeps buzzing every two seconds. I end up having to mute all notifications from the app because it’s so incessant.  

I know you guys aren’t actually going to fix a lot of this stuff because with the nature of using apples interface for recording screen time data, you can’t. I just wanted to put this out there in case some of these issues are fixable. Thank you.

[Edit] thank you for fixing my issue with the iPad version!

I have a new issue that I failed to mention before: the limit on selecting nine is frustrating. You can select more than one category, but if you go into a category to unselect certain apps, then all of the apps that were selected are now counted towards this 49 count limit. Part of the reason I have to unselect categories and select visual apps or websites is because Opal keeps miscategorizing one of my preferred shopping websites under utilities, or some such. reviews.title: Bring back exclusions
reviews.text: I started using this app 12/25, and it was a total game changer for my ADHD. However, it has slowly become less and less effective for me with all the changes and updates. I used to be so proud of my screen time- it was sort of gamified for me, seeing how low I could keep it. There used to be a feature to exclude apps from being included in your screen time, which was a big part of what made the app so effective for me. I was always discouraged seeing a high screen time on my device from apps like maps or Spotify or my audiobook apps, especially because I often forgot to lock my phone. Opal gave you the option to exclude those from contributing to your screen time. I also use a row counting app when I crochet, and it was great to exclude that because I have it open for hours at a time. When the feature was taken away, it was really discouraging to see my screen time shoot up. All of a sudden just having my row counting app open shot my screen time up by hours. Having time that is EXPLICITLY analog and intentionally offline contribute to a previously motivating feature was such a bummer. I feel like the app worked well initially, all of these extra features and changes make it much more unusable for me. I think all of the rapid changes should be introduced slowly. When people find something that works, especially people struggling with attention, the apps influx of changes can be frustrating and render the app less effective. Don’t make changes for changes sake.

reviews.title: Undo the updates
reviews.text: This app was amazing until the recent update changed the UI. It really ruined the app for me. It isn't intuitive anymore. It is very sad because it really helped manage screen time with the previous interface. Now, why is the little unblock oval floating over the Home Screen so prominately? Why stuck in dark mode with sizes of text all over the place? Why are the buttons so small and transparent? It is all now cluttered and hard to find. Also I want to easily start sessions anytime and be able to start simultaneous other block sessions at different lengths. This is not possible now. The single session takes over the whole screen, it doesn't allow access to any other parts of opal when using the instant start blocking feature. This is so bizarre. I want to access the app to review rules, look at settings, etc. not lock the entire app during a session.  It's essentially useless. Please restore what was great about opal.

reviews.title: No paywall. Works
reviews.text: I got this app because I wanted to try something better than screen time limits. What I don’t like about those is that you can avoid them so quickly, and because it’s a system notification, it’s almost second nature. This thing actually works. You can set limits, but also you can create a bunch of other ways to discourage doomscrolling. I like the focus sessions. Another thing that sets this apart from screen time limits, is the small, but effective amount of effort you need in order to reset your limit. If you want to reset it, you have to go to the app, and wait 5 seconds, while it plays a nice ambience on the screen. It’s a nice touch. The second time you reset, it’s 40 seconds. I’ve only ever gotten to that one twice. It’s a very effective system. And you need to show a friend a video, or message someone, there are ways to bypass it. I also love the little achievement gems you get. You have a little collection shelf in the app, and they are actually really neat to look at. Great app, and a lot of features aren’t locked behind a paywall.

To go along with that, when I go in to pause blocking on a certain app there’s a good 40% chance the buttons won’t even work causing me to force close and reopen the app. Overall it’ll help you reduce your screen time, but expect bugs and some frustration with it from time to time.

reviews.title: Pointless updates, need to go back
reviews.text:
Opal team-
There was no reason for you guys to entirely change the UI of this app. This was one of the best functioning, helpful apps that I have ever came across and am currently on a 201 day streak of using the functionalities the app provides. With the change to the UI, it is now super difficult to track the timing spent specific apps, the app blocking only works 50% of the time, the sleep score doesn’t even make sense and shouldn’t be apart of the app, the app isn’t even synced to my real local time (I will get notifications at 11pm that my normal sleep time of 9:37pm is approaching, AND the daily scores will reset at different times every day), and it’s honestly running way slower than before. 

Opal, please just go back to where we can see all of our apps, see how much time spent, and knock it off with all of the unnecessary add ins and extra “scoring tactics”. 

Again, this was my favorite app for a while due to the superb user experience and easy to use app, but has become extremely hard to see the value in continuing to use this app.
